subject: physiology
title: Hormone Receptors, cAMP, IP3-DAG, and Tyrosine Kinase Cascades

steps.tx: Endocrine communication relies upon high-affinity hormone receptors that transduce minute nanomolar circulating chemical signals into profound intracellular biological responses. Hydrophilic peptide hormones and circulating catecholamines cannot penetrate the hydrophobic lipid bilayer, binding instead to specialized cell-surface **transmembrane hormone receptors** on target tissues.
steps.say: Hydrophilic peptides and catecholamines bind surface transmembrane receptors to activate intracellular second messengers.

left.title: Cell-Surface Receptors (Hydrophilic)
points: Peptides, glycoproteins, and catecholamines (adrenaline, TSH, ACTH)
Cannot penetrate lipid bilayer; bind extracellular receptor domains
Rapid onset of action within seconds to minutes
Signal amplified through second messengers (cAMP, IP3, Ca2+)

right.title: Intracellular Receptors (Lipophilic)
points: Steroid hormones, thyroid hormones, and calcitriol (vitamin D)
Diffuses across plasma membrane to bind cytosolic or nuclear receptors
Slow onset of action over hours to days
Acts as ligand-activated transcription factors altering gene expression

steps.tx: The largest class of cell-surface receptors are seven-transmembrane G-protein coupled receptors. In the classic **cyclic AMP signaling pathway**, ligand binding activates stimulatory Gs alpha subunits, which exchange GDP for GTP to activate membrane-bound adenylyl cyclase, converting adenosine triphosphate into cyclic AMP.
steps.say: Gs-coupled receptors stimulate adenylyl cyclase to generate cyclic AMP, which activates protein kinase A.

nodes.label: Hormone Binds Seven-Transmembrane GPCR (e.g., Glucagon, ACTH, TSH, PTH)
Stimulatory Gs Alpha Subunit Releases GDP and Binds GTP
Adenylyl Cyclase Hydrolyzes ATP into Cyclic Adenosine Monophosphate (cAMP)
cAMP Binds Regulatory Subunits of Protein Kinase A (PKA), Activating Catalytic Subunits

steps.tx: Elevated cyclic AMP binds the regulatory subunits of protein kinase A, liberating active catalytic subunits that phosphorylate serine and threonine residues on specific cellular enzymes. Cyclic AMP signaling is terminated by **cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterases**, which hydrolyze cyclic AMP into inactive five-prime adenosine monophosphate.
steps.say: Protein kinase A phosphorylates metabolic enzymes, while phosphodiesterases break down cyclic AMP to stop the signal.

rows: ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH, Glucagon, PTH, ADH (V2)
GnRH, TRH, GHRH, Angiotensin II, ADH (V1), Oxytocin

steps.tx: Receptors coupled to Gq alpha proteins activate membrane-bound phospholipase C-beta, initiating the classical **IP3 and DAG pathway**. Upon activation, phospholipase C hydrolyzes membrane phosphatidylinositol four-five-bisphosphate into two distinct intracellular second messengers: water-soluble inositol one-four-five-trisphosphate and membrane-bound diacylglycerol to coordinate intracellular signal transduction.
steps.say: Gq-coupled receptors activate phospholipase C to split PIP2 into IP3, which mobilizes calcium, and DAG.

nodes.label: Hormone Binds Gq-Coupled Receptor (e.g., TRH, GnRH, Angiotensin II)
Phospholipase C-Beta Hydrolyzes Membrane PIP2 into IP3 and DAG
IP3 Diffuses to Endoplasmic Reticulum, Releasing Intracellular Calcium
Diacylglycerol (DAG) and Calcium Activate Membrane-Bound Protein Kinase C

steps.tx: Inositol trisphosphate diffuses rapidly through cytoplasm to bind ligand-gated calcium channels on the endoplasmic reticulum, releasing stored calcium into the cytosol. Elevated calcium binds the calcium-binding protein calmodulin, forming an active complex that stimulates **calcium-calmodulin-dependent protein kinases** to phosphorylate target cellular enzymes.
steps.say: IP3 releases calcium from endoplasmic reticulum storage, activating calmodulin-dependent kinases.

left.title: Inositol 1,4,5-Trisphosphate (IP3)
points: Binds IP3-gated Ca2+ release channels on endoplasmic reticulum
Elevates cytosolic calcium from 100 nM to micromolar levels
Drives smooth muscle contraction and exocytosis

right.title: Diacylglycerol (DAG)
points: Lipid-soluble messenger retained in plasma membrane
Recruits cytosolic Protein Kinase C (PKC) to membrane
Acts synergistically with calcium to fully activate PKC
Phosphorylates proteins regulating cell growth and proliferation

steps.tx: Unlike G-protein coupled receptors, receptors for insulin and insulin-like growth factor 1 possess intrinsic enzymatic activity within their cytoplasmic domains, operating as **receptor tyrosine kinases**. Ligand binding induces receptor autophosphorylation on tyrosine residues, creating docking sites for insulin receptor substrates.
steps.say: Insulin and IGF-1 receptors have intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity, autophosphorylating docking sites for downstream adapters.

nodes.label: Insulin Binds Extracellular Alpha Subunits of Heterotetrameric Receptor
Beta Subunits Undergo Trans-Autophosphorylation on Specific Tyrosine Residues
Insulin Receptor Substrates (IRS-1 / IRS-2) Bind Phosphotyrosine Pockets
Activation of PI3K-Akt Pathway Drives GLUT4 Translocation and Glycogen Synthesis

steps.tx: Insulin and IGF 1 receptors are **receptor tyrosine kinases**. Ligand binding makes them phosphorylate their own tyrosine residues, building docks for insulin receptor substrates, and the enzyme activity sits in the receptor itself. Growth hormone and prolactin use another receptor class. Each ligand dimerises a cytokine receptor that has no intrinsic kinase. The paired receptors recruit JAK2, JAK2 phosphorylates STAT proteins, and those STATs carry the signal to gene transcription.
steps.say: Insulin and IGF 1 receptors carry their own tyrosine kinase and phosphorylate docking sites for insulin receptor substrates. Growth hormone and prolactin receptors do not. Ligand binding dimerises them, the pair recruits JAK2, and JAK2 activates STAT proteins that move the message into the nucleus.

vis.alt: Growth hormone and prolactin receptors dimerising and recruiting JAK2 to activate STAT proteins.
vis.caption: Paired cytokine receptors for growth hormone and prolactin draw in JAK2, which phosphorylates STAT proteins. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Growth hormone and prolactin receptors have no kinase of their own, so the picture follows what they borrow. Docked **Janus kinase 2** enzymes phosphorylate the receptor and then STAT proteins, which pair up, enter the nucleus and switch on genes for growth and milk production. A broken JAK2 signal therefore weakens both axes at once, while a permanently active JAK2 drives blood cell overproduction in myeloproliferative disease.
steps.say: Growth hormone and prolactin receptors borrow Janus kinase 2, which phosphorylates STAT proteins that enter the nucleus. Active JAK2 signalling drives growth, lactation and, when uncontrolled, blood cell excess.

vis.alt: Diagram of Janus kinase 2 proteins docked under a cytokine receptor, phosphorylating STAT molecules bound for the nucleus.
vis.caption: Docked Janus kinase 2 is shown phosphorylating STAT proteins after growth hormone receptor activation. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Receptors for growth hormone and prolactin belong to the cytokine receptor superfamily, lacking intrinsic enzymatic activity. Ligand binding induces receptor dimerization, recruiting and activating cytoplasmic **Janus kinase 2 proteins**, which phosphorylate signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) proteins that translocate to the nucleus.
steps.say: Growth hormone and prolactin receptors lack kinase activity, using JAK2 to phosphorylate STAT proteins that enter the nucleus.

vis.alt: Growth hormone and prolactin cytokine receptors dimerising to recruit JAK2 and STAT signalling
vis.caption: Growth hormone and prolactin cytokine receptors dimerising to recruit JAK2 and STAT signalling. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Inherited genetic mutations in G-protein alpha subunits produce distinct endocrine diseases. In McCune-Albright syndrome, mosaic postzygotic activating mutations in Gs alpha cause autonomous, ligand-independent cyclic AMP generation, producing precocious puberty, polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, and café-au-lait skin pigmentation via unrestrained **constitutive Gs signaling**.
steps.say: McCune-Albright syndrome is caused by mosaic activating Gs mutations, causing precocious puberty and fibrous bone lesions.

vis.alt: Multiple endocrine neoplasia and receptor signaling mutations
vis.caption: Neuroendocrine receptor tyrosine kinase mutations, G-protein signaling, and polyglandular syndromes.
